newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys will submit the government's new bill on fines for tax offenders in Parliament on Monday. Among the new provisions in the bill are the writing off of almost half outstanding debts to the state, more favourable terms for settlement of debts and stricter provisions for the non-payment of Value Added Tax.

--The second public share from Greek telecoms organisation OTE has not brought the expected improvement in climate on the Athens Stock Exchange despsite its massive success. In fact, the bourse came under intense selling pressure last week from middle-range private and foreign institutional investors with shares in OTE, banks and blue chips.

--The government is preparing to reveal its new development strategy, developed by a special national economy ministry committee. The new plans include replacing free subsidies with subsidised interest rates and tax relief, changes to subsidy percentages for farming zones and special incentives for certain investments involving advanced technology or environmental protections.
--The foodstuffs sector has once again proved itself the leader in Greek industry with the 120 firms posting profits of over 100 million drachmas each.

--National Bank of Greece will lead the way for other Greek banks in forex lending worth one trillion drachmas to the state and public enterprises and organisations. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
